subject: Game Theory
title: Electoral System Design
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Electoral System Design.

hook.text: New Zealand switched from first-past-the-post to proportional representation in 1996. Politics transformed overnight.

buildup.text: Electoral systems shape party structure. Plurality systems create two parties; proportional ones create many.

discovery.text: Each system trades off representativeness against governability. More parties mean more voices but harder coalitions.

twist.text: No system is neutral. Every rule advantages some groups and disadvantages others. Design is political.

climax.text: Countries rarely change systems because those in power were elected by the current rules.

punchline.text: The rules decide who can win.

quiz.question: Why do countries rarely change their electoral systems?
options: Those in power benefit from the current system
